# Laptop Guard v11.1.0

This is the first formal GitHub release checkpoint for the already-versioned `11.1.0` codebase.

It establishes a stable baseline before the v11.2 setup/security hardening milestone and the staged architecture evolution work.

## Product baseline

Laptop Guard is an owner-controlled Linux security agent with guarded remote control, local-only operation support, camera/input monitoring, evidence capture, warning/lock response, event history, chat/audio/TTS helpers, service/autostart support, and guided setup/diagnostics.

Security-sensitive operations remain constrained by owner authorization, explicit configuration, confirmation/opt-in rules, and local privacy/security boundaries. The project does not intentionally expose a generic remote shell or arbitrary command execution surface.

## Repository and engineering baseline

This release also establishes the repository-management foundation used for future work:

- GitHub Actions CI across the supported Python matrix;
- repository secret/private-key safety checks;
- Dependabot configuration;
- issue/PR templates, CODEOWNERS, contribution and security policies;
- Codex/AI repository instructions, scoped agents, reusable skills, hooks, and reusable prompt library;
- feature lifecycle and bug-triage maintenance playbooks;
- canonical modular-monolith/ports-and-adapters architecture blueprint;
- dependency-boundary guidance, runtime/security flow diagrams, evolution plan, and ADRs;
- project roadmap and architecture backlog issues.

## Security note

The current repository no longer requires a tracked project `.env` file and repository checks block common local secret artifacts. Any real credential that may have existed in historical Git commits must still be treated as exposed and rotated before the related hardening issue is considered complete.

## Known follow-up work

The next product milestone is **v11.2 — Setup & Security Hardening**:

- #1 credential/history cleanup and rotation;
- #2 resilient self-diagnosing installation;
- #3 actionable readiness/doctor checks.

The architecture evolution track begins with:

- #19 intrusion-response orchestration extraction;
- #20 provider/runtime transport consolidation;
- #21 durable important owner delivery.

See `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `docs/architecture/EVOLUTION_PLAN.md` for the current plans.

## Validation baseline

Repository CI and Repository Safety were green immediately before this release-management work. Hardware/session/provider behavior still requires the target-device validation described in `docs/TESTING.md`.
